title: Uncovering the mechanisms responsible for intravenous paracetamol-induced hypotension
projectDescription: Intravenous (IV) administration of paracetamol (APAP) is well-documented to cause severe hypotension, particularly in critically ill patients. We have previously shown that a metabolite of APAP – N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine (NAPQI) – is a potent vasodilator, but whether APAP can be metabolised to NAPQI in the vasculature is unknown. Here, we show that NAPQI can be generated by the human coronary endothelial cells (HCAECs) treated with APAP, by staining for APAP-adducts and showing a drop in cell viability and glutathione levels, similar to direct NAPQI treatment. We show that glutathione depletion following APAP treatment is caused the cytochrome p450 enzymes (CYPs) expressed in HCAECs by utilizing a blocker of the CYPs, ketoconazole. Furthermore, mass spectrometry analysis of HCAECs treated with 10 mM APAP for 24h shows upregulation of proteins involved in redox biology and the pentose phosphate pathway, as well as CYP20A1 and POR. Lastly, we show that myeloperoxidase can also metabolize APAP to NAPQI at physiologically relevant concentrations. Taken together, this study shows that APAP can be metabolized within the vasculature to the potent vasodilator NAPQI. We suggest that this is the mechanism by which critically ill patients can present with IV APAP-induced hypotension.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Protein was isolated from 0 and 10 mM APAP treated (24 h) HCAEC by lysing the cells in RIPA buffer followed by sonication. Protein quantified was done by Bradford assay (BioRad) according to manufacturer’s instructions.  A total of 20 µg protein diluted in 40 µL RIPA was subjected to heat-treatment for 5 min at 95 °C and placed on ice. Proteins were reduced and alkylated with reduced and alkylated in digestion buffer containing 1:50 (v:v) tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (0.5 M, Sigma) and 1:10 (v:v) 2-chloroacetamide (0.5 M, Sigma) for 30 min at 37 °C. Proteins were captured and digested on paramagnetic beads according to the protein aggregation capture protocol. On-bead digestion was carried out overnight at 37 °C using 0.8 μg Typsin/LysC mix (Promega) in a 1:20 v:v ratio. The peptide-containing solutions were cleaned-up using homemade stage-tips containing a Poly-styrene-divinylbenzene copolymer modified with sulfonic acid groups (SDB-RPS; 3M) material, as described previously. After vacuum centrifugation, samples were resuspended in 2% acetonitrile (Sigma) / 0.1% TFA (Sigma).
dataProcessingProtocol: Bruker raw files (.d) were analyzed with DIA-NN software (v.1.8.0) using the UniProtKB Homo sapiens database (downloaded April 2022). In DIA-NN, the options ‘FASTA digest for library-free search/library generation’ and ‘Deep learning-based spectra, RTs and IMs prediction’ were enabled to generate a library. All other settings were left to default: Digestion protease = Trypsin/P; missed cleavage = 1; max number of variable modifications = 0; N-term M excision = True; C carbamidomethylation = True; peptide length range = 7-30; precursor charge range = 1-4; precursor m/z range = 300-1800; fragment ion m/z range = 200-1800; Precursor FDR (%) = 1%; Use isotopologues = enabled; MBR = enabled; Neural network classifier = single-pass mode; Protein inference = Genes; Quantification strategy = Any LC (high accuracy); Cross-run normalisation = RT-dependent; Library generation = Smart profiling; Speed and RAM usage = Optimal results.  Unique proteins at 1 % FDR were found by DIA-NN software. Protein quantities were generated and obtained from the unique gene list (report.unique-genes.matrix.tsv) and transferred to Perseus (v1.6.14.0). The Data matrix was reduced by filtering for minimum three valid values in each group and subjected to a two-sided student’s T-test in Perseus between the treated and untreated group.  Up- and downregulated genes were subjected to analysis in Cytoscape (v3.10.1) with the String software. To functionally generate networks the confidence interval was set to 0.6 and subjected to MCL clustering (inflation value = 2.5, Array source = stringdb::score) based on literature-based protein-protein interaction. The up- and downregulated genes were color coded with shades of red and blue, respectively to signify the level of regulation. Enrichment analysis was generated on the clusters with more than 10 nodes for molecular function with a cutoff FDR<0.01 and max. 10 molecular functions with the lowest FDR is shown for each cluster.
